verses.text: The LORD appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre. Abraham was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them, and bowed low to the ground.
He said, "My lord, if you are pleased with me, please do not pass by your servant.
Let me have a little water brought, so that you can all wash your feet and rest under this tree.
Let me get you something to eat, so that you can be refreshed before you go on your way. You have come to your servant, after all." "Very well," they answered. "Do as you say."
So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said. "Get three large measures of the best flour, knead it and bake some bread."
Then he ran to the herd and chose a fine, tender calf. He gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
Then he brought some butter and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and set them in front of the men. While they ate, he stood near them under the tree.
"Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked him. "There, in the tent," he said.
Then the LORD said, "I will surely come back to you about this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, which was behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were already very old, and Sarah was far too old to have children.
So Sarah laughed to herself as she thought, "After I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really have this joy?"
Then the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Will I really have a baby, now that I am old?'
Is anything too hard for the LORD? I will come back to you at the set time next year, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, "I did not laugh." But he said, "Yes, you did laugh."
Then the men got up to leave, and they looked down towards Sodom. Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way.
Then the LORD said, "Should I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and all nations on earth will be blessed through him.

I have chosen him so that he will teach his children and his family after him to live the way the LORD wants, by doing what is right and fair. Then the LORD will do for Abraham what he has promised him."
Then the LORD said, "The cry against Sodom and Gomorrah is very loud, and their sin is very serious.
I will go down and see if what they have done is as bad as the cry that has reached me. If not, I will know."
The men turned away and went towards Sodom, but Abraham stayed standing in front of the LORD.
Then Abraham came near to him and said, "Will you really destroy good people along with the wicked?
What if there are fifty good people in the city? Will you really destroy it and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty good people in it?

Surely you would never do such a thing, killing good people together with the wicked, treating the good and the wicked alike! Surely you would never do that! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?"
The LORD said, "If I find fifty good people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."
Then Abraham spoke up again: "I am nothing but dust and ashes, yet I have been bold enough to speak to the Lord.
What if there are only forty-five good people instead of fifty? Will you destroy the whole city because five are missing?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it."
Once again Abraham spoke to him: "What if only forty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of the forty, I will not do it."
Then Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord, but let me speak. What if only thirty can be found there?" He answered, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."
Abraham said, "Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, what if only twenty can be found there?" He said, "For the sake of the twenty, I will not destroy it."
Then Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord, but let me speak just once more. What if only ten can be found there?" He answered, "For the sake of the ten, I will not destroy it."
When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, he went on his way, and Abraham went back home.
